items.title: RIKEN publishes recap of RIKEN Mathematics & AI Symposium 2026
items.summary_en: RIKEN published a recap of the RIKEN Mathematics & AI Symposium 2026, an international symposium held August 18-21, 2026 at RIKEN's Tokyo campus and jointly hosted by RIKEN AIP, the RIKEN Pioneering Research Institute (PRI), and the RIKEN Mathematical, Computational and Information Science Domain. About 300 participants (in-person and online) discussed topics including AI-assisted mathematical discovery, using mathematical theory to improve understanding of AI reliability, and formalization/proof.
items.notes: Original language: Japanese/English bilingual RIKEN site; summarized in English here. Content verified only via WebSearch snippets -- direct access to riken.jp was blocked by the collection environment's egress proxy (third consecutive run with RIKEN/UTokyo domains blocked). The symposium itself ran Aug 18-21, 2026 (before this run's collection window), but this recap article was published Sept 4, 2026, within window.

items.title: RIKEN AIP announces Tokyo will host COLT 2027
items.summary_en: RIKEN AIP's news page announced that the 40th Annual Conference on Learning Theory (COLT 2027), a leading international venue for theoretical machine learning research, will be held in Tokyo from June 28 to July 2, 2027. Hosting the event underscores RIKEN AIP's standing in the international computational/statistical learning theory community.
items.notes: Exact article URL/slug could not be confirmed because aip.riken.jp is blocked by the collection environment's egress proxy for the third consecutive run; found only via a WebSearch snippet referencing an announcement posted 2026-09-07 on aip.riken.jp/news. The URL given here is the general news-listing page, not the specific article -- flag for re-verification once direct access is restored.

items.title: UTokyo Matsuo-Iwasawa Lab publishes fall 2026 AI/data-science course lineup
items.summary_en: The University of Tokyo's Matsuo-Iwasawa Laboratory (Matsuo Lab) published its lineup of AI and data-science courses opening in autumn 2026, continuing its practice of offering 30+ courses per year on topics such as large language model applications and physical-AI robotics. The lab separately flagged its 'GENIAC PRIZE 2026' contest, with an individual-member application deadline of September 30, 2026.
